name: SynthID Remover
description: Regenerate pixels to break invisible AI watermarks

paragraphs: Upload an image you generated yourself and get back a PNG with no metadata and a regenerated pixel layer. A before and after slider shows what changed.

SynthID is Google DeepMind's watermark for AI-generated images, audio, text and video. It is built into the pixels and is invisible to people (source). OpenAI's verifier checks for it, and that page is the only checker this Space was tested against.

The C2PA, EXIF and XMP metadata disappear because the output is a fresh PNG. The invisible watermark lives in the pixels, so the pixels are redrawn. The app encodes the image, noises it part of the way, and denoises it again with Qwen-Image-2.1.
features: Subtle (default) redraws the image at 17 steps, lines the redraw up halfway with your original, then takes only the 16 to 32 px luma band from it. Every other pixel and all the color stay yours, so faces and structure…
Strong returns the full redraw after 17 steps. It removed the mark on each of three images, but it rewrites the image, including faces.
